Why the 08:14 is always late: a timetable read closely

The 08:14 from Winterthur is timetabled to reach Zurich at 08:31. It reaches Zurich at 08:34, and it has done so on four days in five for two years. Nothing is broken. The timetable is simply describing a train that does not exist.

Between Effretikon and Dietlikon the line carries three services in the same seventeen minutes. The 08:14 is the third of them, and it inherits every second the first two lose. A timetable that adds no slack anywhere is a timetable that hands its debts downhill.

The fix is unglamorous and well understood: move the 08:14 to 08:16, accept a worse connection at Oerlikon for eleven passengers, and give the whole corridor back its ninety seconds. It has been proposed twice.

The proposals are public. Reading them takes an afternoon, and the afternoon is the point: nobody who has read them thinks the 08:14 is a mystery.
